title: "R for data analysis"

description: "Six sessions to learn R: import, manipulate, describe, visualise and report development data."
---

This course is for **Master GPE** students (development economics). There are **no prerequisites**: we start from zero, install R, write our first lines of code, and finish with a reproducible report.

One development question runs through all six sessions, the **common thread** of the course:

> **Growth, health and inequality: what does the data say about developing countries?**

We start with three countries (United States, China, India), then move to all countries in the world using World Bank data. The last session ends with a figure for a "briefing note to the minister".

## Before the first session

::: {.callout-important}
## To do at home

1. Install **R**: <https://cran.r-project.org/>.
2. Install **RStudio Desktop**: <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/> (after R).
3. In RStudio: *File > New Project > New Directory* and create a project folder named `r-course`.
4. Download **[data.zip](data.zip)** and unzip it **into the `r-course` folder**, so that `data/` and `R/theme_cours.R` sit next to the `.Rproj` file (`here::here()` relies on this).
5. Install the packages: paste the block below in the RStudio **Console** and run it **once**. It takes a few minutes.
:::

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "here", "janitor", "readxl", "writexl",
                   "lubridate", "scales", "WDI", "gt", "fixest",
                   "modelsummary", "ggrepel", "sf", "rnaturalearth",
                   "rnaturalearthdata", "patchwork", "plotly", "crosstalk",
                   "shiny"))
```

Expected folder tree:

```
r-course/
├── r-course.Rproj
├── data/
│   ├── wdi_panel.csv
│   ├── ...
│   └── raw/
└── R/
    └── theme_cours.R
```

## How to use this site

- Every session follows the same plan: objectives, explanations with code, **exercises**, then "Key takeaways".
- Type the code yourself in RStudio rather than copying it: that is how you learn.
- **Solutions are collapsed**: try first, then open to compare.
- An error is not a failure: read the message, it almost always says what is wrong.

## AI and code

AI assistants can explain an error message or an unfamiliar function. They must not replace your learning. **Always run the suggested code and understand every line** before using it: code that runs is not necessarily correct.
